title: feat(scripts): Arkham intel-marathon pass 2 — populatedTags fix, cross-chain discovery, quota-aware sweep

findings.author: claude[bot]
findings.title: [P1] flushWrites() permanently drops a whole batch of already-attested writes on any transient Upstash failure, and the circuit breaker won't catch it
findings.body:
**[P1] `flushWrites()` permanently drops a whole batch of already-attested writes on any transient Upstash failure, and the circuit breaker won't catch it.**

`pendingWrites.splice(0, pendingWrites.length)` (line 921) removes the batch from the queue *before* `flushNewWrites`/`flushRefreshWrites` make the network call. If `pipeline()` throws (network blip, Upstash 5xx, a single command's `.error`), the whole batch — up to `HSET_BATCH` (100) entries — is lost: nothing is retried, and there's no code path that puts it back.

This is worse than a one-off loss because every address in that batch already has a `{address, status}` line in `progressFile` from the per-address loop (line 1010), written *before* the flush is attempted. On resume, `processed` (built from `progressFile`, lines 804-818) treats those addresses as done, so they're never retried — the label write for a fully-fetched, quality-gate-passed address is gone for good.

It also can't self-report: the `catch` at line 1014 attributes the flush error to whatever address happens to be mid-iteration and calls `noteFailure()`, but `recordResult()` (line 973) resets `consecutiveErrors = 0` on every successful Arkham fetch, which runs *before* the next flush attempt. So a sustained Upstash outage never accumulates `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS` — the run keeps calling Arkham (burning the 10k-lookup trial quota) for the full queue while silently writing nothing, and the circuit breaker built to catch exactly this kind of "API stopped working" scenario never trips.

Given the 70+ minute / 68k-address unattended run this is designed for, and that the whole point of the CAS/HSETNX design is race-safety across that window, this seems worth fixing before a full production run: retry the flush (or re-queue the batch back into `pendingWrites` on failure) rather than discarding it, and/or don't record `{address, status}` as "processed" until the corresponding write has actually landed.

[Fix this →](https://claude.ai/code?q=In%20ui-dashboard%2Fscripts%2Fintel-marathon%2Ftier1-bulk-enrich.mjs%2C%20on%20branch%20feat%2Fintel-pass-2%3A%20flushWrites()%20around%20line%20919-926%20splices%20pendingWrites%20before%20calling%20flushNewWrites%2FflushRefreshWrites%2C%20so%20if%20the%20Upstash%20pipeline%20call%20throws%20the%20whole%20batch%20of%20writes%20is%20permanently%20lost%20-%20and%20since%20each%20address%20already%20has%20a%20%7Baddress%2C%20status%7D%20line%20in%20the%20progress%20file%20written%20before%20the%20flu

findings.author: claude[bot]
findings.title: [P2] HARDPAGECAP truncation isn't treated as an incomplete-discovery source, even though it is one.
findings.body:
**[P2] `HARD_PAGE_CAP` truncation isn't treated as an incomplete-discovery source, even though it is one.**

`discoverAll()` aborts the run when a source **errors** (`failedSources`, checked here), matching the header comment's "a partial set looks identical to full coverage afterwards." But `pageSource()` can also return `capped: true` when a single source exceeds `HARD_PAGE_CAP` (250k rows) — that's logged as a `⚠ HARD_PAGE_CAP hit — truncated` warning (line 286) and otherwise ignored; it doesn't join `failedSources` and doesn't trigger the abort/`--allow-partial-discovery` gate.

That's the same failure mode the abort exists to prevent — a silently incomplete discovery set — just triggered by row count instead of an exception. Low risk at today's scale (68,433 total addresses, well under any single source's cap), but if it's hit it'd defeat the "abort rather than sweep partial" guarantee this function otherwise enforces.

findings.author: coderabbitai[bot]
findings.title: Match the exact tfvars key.
findings.body:
**Match the exact tfvars key.**

Line 60 matches any key that starts with `$tfkey`. For example, `arkham_api_key_backup` can supply `ARKHAM_API_KEY` when it appears before `arkham_api_key`. Require whitespace and `=` after the key.

✅ Addressed in commits 0754c83 to 5f9e96a

findings.author: coderabbitai[bot]
findings.title: Cap unique tags in both sanitizers.
findings.body:
**Cap unique tags in both sanitizers.**

The shared helper uses the same slice-before-dedup order. If `MAX_TAGS_COUNT` means 20 unique tags, move the slice after dedup in both implementations. Otherwise, retain the current order and remove this concern. Refresh merges can let duplicate or blank tags consume the 20-item window and discard later unique tags.

✅ Addressed in commits 0754c83 to 5f9e96a

findings.author: coderabbitai[bot]
findings.title: A failed flush discards the pending batch and marks the addresses as processed.
findings.body:
**A failed flush discards the pending batch and marks the addresses as processed.**

`flushWrites` splices the batch out of `pendingWrites` before it calls `pipeline`. `pipeline` throws on a transport error or on any per-command error. The spliced entries are then unreachable, so up to `HSET_BATCH` enrichment results are lost.

Two call sites make the loss silent:

- Line 1012 calls `flushWrites` inside the per-address `try`. An Upstash failure is caught by the `catch` at Line 1014, recorded against the current address as an Arkham error, and counted by `noteFailure`. The run continues.
- Every address in the lost batch already has a `{address, status}` line in `progressFile`, so the resume filter at Line 854 skips it on the next run. The addresses are never re-enriched, and their quota is already spent.

Restore the batch on failure so a later flush retries it.

✅ Addressed in commits 0754c83 to 5f9e96a

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.title: Preserve Tier 2 tags when merging capped labels
findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve Tier 2 tags when merging capped labels**

For addresses whose Tier 1 entry already contains 20 tags—which this change now makes possible by restoring `populatedTags`—appending Arkham tags after `ctp:` and `type:` here does not preserve the forensic tags. The write path later builds a set with `existingEntry.tags` first and slices it to 20, so the newly derived counterparty and contract tags fall beyond the cap and are silently discarded. Prioritize those derived tags again when merging with the existing entry so the light-forensic pass records its results for richly tagged addresses.

findings.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
findings.title: Abort when discovery reaches the hard page cap
findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Abort when discovery reaches the hard page cap**

When any discovery source exceeds 250,000 rows, `pageSource` returns `capped: true`, but this branch only prints a warning and never adds the source to `failedSources`. The default run therefore proceeds without `--allow-partial-discovery` and spends Arkham quota on a silently truncated registry, contrary to the new fail-closed discovery behavior. Treat a capped source as incomplete and abort unless partial discovery was explicitly allowed.

findings.author: cursor[bot]
findings.title: Refresh wipes forensic tags
findings.body:
### Refresh wipes forensic tags **High Severity** `buildWriteEntry` unions `fresh.tags` ahead of the existing tag list, then `sanitizeEntry` keeps only the first 20. Arkham often returns enough ids to fill that cap alone, so a refresh drops prior `ctp:` / `type:` forensic tags that tier2 wrote into `labels`. Pass-2 refreshes therefore undo tier2 attribution for heavily tagged addresses.
